newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar emir tells new cabinet to boost development.
newsitem.headline: Qatar emir tells new cabinet to boost development.

text.p: Qatar's emir on Wednesday appointed a new cabinet for the oil and gas-producing Gulf Arab state in which the oil, foreign, finance, defence and interior portfolios remained unchanged.

"At the top of the duties of the new cabinet is continuing the economic, social and cultural development plans...And giving them a new boost," Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani told the cabinet at its first meeting.
The official Qatar News Agency quoted him as urging the ministers to work hard to carry Qatar to the next century.
He said Qatar spent billions of dollars on its gas industry "amidst hard economic and financial conditions...which still prevail despite the recent improvement in oil prices".

According to several decrees setting up the 20-member cabinet by Sheikh Hamad, 15 ministers, including the emir himself as defence minister, remained in the cabinet. Five new ministers were named and four were dropped.
Qatar is a small oil exporter whose native population of 120,000 is among the world's richest with per capita gross national product of $22,000. Some 440,000 foreigners work there.

Oil reserves of Qatar, which is a member of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), are overshadowed by its natural gas deposits which are exceeded only by those of Russia and Iran. It is due to start export of liquefied natural gas in December.
Diplomats said most of the new ministers were Western educated and under 40-years-old. Most of the ministers who lost their jobs were heavily involved in business in Qatar.
The emir last week named his third son, Sheikh Jassim bin Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani, 18, as Crown Prince.
Officials and diplomats said the appointments consolidated the power of the emir, who last year ousted his father Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad al-Thani in a bloodless palace coup.

The decrees said Prime Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Khalifa al-Thani, appointed on Tuesday, retains his post as Interior Minister. Influential Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani remains Foreign Minister while Sheikh Mohammad bin Khalifa al-Thani remains Finance, Economy and Trade Minister.
Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah keeps his Energy and Industry portfolio in charge of the vital oil and gas sectors.
A new ministry, the Housing and Civil Services Ministry, was introduced and the Information Ministry was abolished.
The decree said the appointments were made "upon the suggestion of the prime minister".
The cabinet has four ministers of state without portfolio.
Officials and diplomats said moves to create a supreme energy council in place of the Oil Ministry have now been put on hold pending further discussions by officials.

The emir last week issued decrees separating the rime minister's office and the royal court or emiri diwan. Ministers will be appointed at the recommendation of the prime minister and the cabinet will be collectively responsible to the emir.
Under a provisional constitution in force since 1971, the emir acted as his own prime minister. Ministers were appointed and fired at his discretion.
